# Native bitmap entry mock boundaries

These NEW overlays replace only the external composition, loader, startup, generated facts/plan and runner seams while the new entry fixture includes the actual shared native bitmap entry. Existing terminal fixtures are read-only patterns and are not dependencies of this fixture. Real GUI boundary values, provider C headers and independent profile validators remain in the compile.

The selected generated-facts overlay exposes only the selected pixel or actions symbol. Define `FOUNDATION_APPENDED_ENGINE_NATIVE_PROFILE_ENABLED=1`, select `FOUNDATION_APPENDED_ENGINE_NATIVE_DOCUMENT_ACTIONS_PROFILE=0` or `1`, and provide the quoted `FOUNDATION_APPENDED_ENGINE_NATIVE_RUNTIME_HINT`. Each scenario needs a fresh process. Web has no module-factory definition; explicit both supplies a counted factory.

The loader returns a unique synthetic provider token; bind must receive that token and the original Owner. The mock Driver and facade preserve the same Owner/Driver identities. Counters and ordered events distinguish failed prerequisites from later effects. Assertions use explicit exceptions and remain active in optimized builds.

The process-lived mock Driver intentionally retains Owner and wake-token storage. Therefore a zero Owner-destruction count after bind cannot prove production facade/App/port quarantine. These entry fixtures prove only their named boundary identity, ordering, scheduling and forbidden cleanup calls. Actual facade lifetime and native presentation have separate tests. The trivial provider token is not an OS handle and establishes neither DSO unloading nor native-loader behavior.

The mock load plan contains the target/facts/hash joins and explicit root used by the entry. Its exact comparison between verification and loading detects substitution at this seam; it does not execute complete installed-asset inventory verification. That remains the actual loader's separate contract and fixture scope.

No engine, SDK, browser, native DSO, interpreter, payload executable, display, OS input method or actual installed runtime is used. Synthetic source identities and real source-validator success are not retained-input admission or qualification. No command may compile or run these fixtures until the production entry/facade APIs and complete include inputs are frozen by the parent.

The optional `thin/` include overlay declares only the exact SDL/FLTK/Rev three-argument typed factory runner signatures. Compile each actual thin main with `-fsyntax-only`, this overlay first, and the same explicit startup/provider/facade overlays to check its shared-entry wiring. These declarations provide no definitions and must never be counted as an executed runner, actual backend syntax qualification or successful link. The framebuffer thin main can instead receive a separate syntax-only check with the actual generic framebuffer peer and immutable retained GUI headers, without opening an output or running an event loop.

`framebuffer/render_loop_test.cpp` includes the actual framebuffer main and calls its render loop using an explicit fake Session/output overlay. The three fresh-process cases are `success`, `error-frame` (ready frame and failure together, followed by a clean completed close), and `error-detached` (first frame succeeds, then completion and error together). They discriminate failure precedence and retained-artifact ordering. The synthetic Session performs no real App construction, retirement or Surface publication, and its output never touches the filesystem; these cases cannot substitute for actual framebuffer peer, renderer or provider tests.

The metadata-close successor keeps Driver detach separate from facade completion. `runner-detached-without-shutdown` returns before App close; `runner-detached-metadata-debt` returns after Driver detach with a pending App receipt; both require root failure and no cleanup exports after the GUI attempt. `runner-detached-metadata-drained` settles that synthetic receipt during a later App-only turn and permits success without another Driver tick. These fakes discriminate entry receipt accounting; they do not prove actual metadata rendering or App retirement.

The UTF-8 path successor links the actual pure `src/appended/abi.cpp` validator through the real Registry declaration header; it creates no Registry or provider. Native root/output path checks round-trip two-, three- and four-byte scalars through filesystem UTF-8 APIs. Overlong, surrogate, truncated, out-of-range and stray-continuation argv bytes must fail before payload loading. A direct path-helper case also rejects empty and embedded-NUL string views. These are native entry argument tests; the Windows wide-argv bridge and OS Unicode APIs require their own evidence.
